statement: For every positive integer \(n\), define \(P(n)\) as follows: for each prime divisor \(p\) of \(n\), consider the largest integer \(k\) such that \(p^k \leq n\), and sum all such \(p^k\). For example, for \(n = 100 = 2^2 \cdot 5^2\): since \(2^6 < 100 < 2^7\) and \(5^2 < 100 < 5^3\), we get \(P(100) = 2^6 + 5^2 = 89\). Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers \(n\) such that \(P(n) > n\).

Determine all positive integers \(n\) such that the numbers from 1 to \(n\) can be arranged in some order \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n\) with the property that \(k \mid x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k\) for all \(1 \leq k \leq n\).

Given a square \(ABCD\), consider an equilateral triangle \(KLM\) whose vertices \(K\), \(L\), and \(M\) lie on sides \(AB\), \(BC\), and \(CD\) respectively. Find the locus of the midpoints of segment \(KL\) as the equilateral triangle \(KLM\) varies over all such positions.

Consider a \(1000 \times 1000\) board with \(1000000\) unit cells. A piece placed on a cell threatens all cells that are inside a \(19 \times 19\) square centered on that cell and with sides parallel to the board, except for cells in the same row or the same column as the piece. Determine the maximum number of pieces that can be placed on the board so that no two pieces threaten each other.
Find all pairs of positive integers \(x, y\) such that \(x^3 + y^3 = 4(x^2 y + xy^2 - 5)\).

For every positive integer \(n\), consider the polynomial of degree \(2n\) with real coefficients
\[P(x) = a_{2n}x^{2n} + a_{2n-1}x^{2n-1} + \cdots + a_1 x + a_0\]
where all coefficients satisfy \(100 \leq a_i \leq 101\) for \(0 \leq i \leq 2n\). Find the smallest possible value of \(n\) such that \(P(x)\) can have at least one real root.
